sources.entry: Coordinated and Efficient Huge Page Management with Ingens - Measures the fault latency, memory bloat and unfairness that eager THP promotion causes, and shows what removes them.

summary.title: Coordinated and Efficient Huge Page Management with Ingens
summary.one_liner: Ingens shows how an OS can manage transparent huge pages in a coordinated way, treating contiguity as a first-class resource, to cut fairness problems, tail latency and memory bloat.
takeaways: Eager transparent huge page promotion causes fault latency, memory bloat and unfairness between applications.
Ingens treats physical contiguity as a first-class resource and tracks memory utilization and access frequency to decide huge page allocation.
Reported results from the prototype include up to 18% performance gain, up to 41% tail-latency reduction, and memory bloat reduced from 69% to under 1% for Redis and Cloudstone.
The design relies on a small set of basic primitives coordinated across the OS rather than best-effort spot fixes.
summary.summary: The paper argues that current OS and hypervisor huge page support is a set of best-effort algorithms that cause fairness and performance pathologies. It presents Ingens, a framework that provides transparent huge page support using a few basic primitives, managing contiguity as a first-class resource and tracking page utilization and access frequency. The authors evaluate a prototype on Web services (Cloudstone) and the Redis key-value store, reporting fairness gains, up to 18% performance improvement, up to 41% tail-latency reduction, and memory bloat reduced from 69% to under 1%. The page is the USENIX OSDI 2016 paper listing with abstract and BibTeX.
